```
murshid/
├─ src/murshid/
│  ├─ llm/                the model boundary
│  │  ├─ interfaces.py    LLMClient, LLMRequest, LLMResponse, StreamChunk, LLMError
│  │  ├─ openai_compat.py OpenAI cloud, the gateway, and vLLM — one adapter
│  │  ├─ anthropic_client.py  the Messages dialect and its five differences
│  │  ├─ resilient.py     retry + fallback, once, for everything
│  │  ├─ fake.py          the third implementation: scripted, deterministic, free
│  │  └─ tokens.py        counting per route, with the route's own encoding
│  ├─ prompts/
│  │  ├─ registry.py      load_prompt("answer_faq.v5"), the canary, typed variables
│  │  └─ library/         versioned artefacts with front matter and changelogs
│  ├─ guards/
│  │  ├─ input_guards.py  three layers, cheapest first
│  │  ├─ output_guards.py canary · outbound PII · internals · relayed instructions
│  │  └─ refusals.py      designed, bilingual, never an echo of the payload
│  ├─ domain/
│  │  ├─ directory.py     the only trusted source of service facts
│  │  ├─ ticket.py        the output contract, and the validators a schema cannot express
│  │  └─ session.py       windowed state, the PII vault, and the authorisation gate
│  ├─ tools/
│  │  ├─ registry.py      three tools, one per risk class, with the class in code
│  │  └─ services.py      the systems behind them (and one poisoned note field)
│  ├─ pipeline/
│  │  ├─ assemble.py      guard | route | (faq | service | escalate) | guard
│  │  ├─ structured.py    validate → retry → repair, used by everything structured
│  │  ├─ tool_loop.py     the course's one agentic loop — bounded, authorised, traced
│  │  ├─ faq.py           the cacheable prefix, and the cascade
│  │  ├─ service.py       the workflow with the tool loop inside it
│  │  ├─ router.py        the biggest cost lever, and an eval-gated one
│  │  └─ groundedness.py  one deterministic check, used in three places
│  ├─ caching/            exact and semantic tiers, with safe keys
│  ├─ observability/      structured logging, and the cost meter
│  ├─ api/main.py         a thin FastAPI layer over the same pipeline
│  ├─ app.py              the composition root — the ONE place concretes meet
│  └─ cli.py              ask · chat · stream · doctor
├─ infra/mockgw/          the course gateway (a simulator)
├─ eval/                  golden set · harness · gate · judge calibration · report
├─ scripts/               every measurement the labs take
├─ data/                  corpora, all generated from curated seeds
└─ tests/                 165 tests, offline
```

## The rule

**Application code depends on protocols and configuration. Only `app.py` knows
about concrete classes.**

That is what makes the substitution in Module 1 real:

```bash
export MURSHID_PRIMARY_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1
export MURSHID_PRIMARY_API_KEY=sk-...
make eval        # nothing in src/ changed
```

Three tests enforce it, in `tests/test_architecture.py`:

| Test | What fails without it |
|---|---|
| `test_no_provider_sdk_outside_the_adapters` | a config change becomes a six-week rewrite |
| `test_no_inline_prompt_text_in_code` | "what changed?" stops being answerable |
| `test_every_llm_request_bounds_max_tokens` | a demo default becomes a production incident |

## Reading order, if you are new to it

1. `llm/interfaces.py` — everything the application is allowed to know.
2. `app.py` — how a route name becomes an adapter, and how the five stages get
   wired.
3. `pipeline/assemble.py` — the request path, in one screen.
4. `pipeline/structured.py` — the loop that Modules 3, 4 and 5 all reuse.
5. `guards/input_guards.py` — read the comments; several of them are scars.
6. `infra/mockgw/app/brain.py` — read the module docstring before anything else.

## Where the numbers come from

| Artefact | Generated by |
|---|---|
| `BENCHMARKS.md` | hand-written, but every row names the command that produced it |
| `EVALUATION_REPORT.md` | `make eval-report`, from whatever is in `eval/out/` |
| `eval/golden/regression_set.yaml` | `make golden` — edit the seeds, not the file |
| `eval/golden/human_labels_40.jsonl` | `python eval/build_human_labels.py` |
| `data/*.jsonl`, `data/tokenizer_pairs.csv` | `make corpora` |
| `eval/baseline.json` | `make baseline LABEL=...` — a governed act |

Regenerating a corpus or a baseline is deliberate, diffable and explained in the
commit message. That is the same discipline the golden set demands of the labs, and
the repository holds itself to it.
